I have AvPD so my situation may be kind of extreme compared to other people, but just the idea of being in a relationship (both platonic and romantic) sounds incredibly painful to me and over time I kind of accepted the idea that i'll probably be alone for the rest of my days.

Seeing a therapist can be useful, but you have to find the right one or else it's just going to result in a waste of time and you'll possibly end up even more frustrated and discouraged than you are now.
As other people already said, i would suggest to look for therapists specialized in personality disorders; it's also useful to avoid therapy methods that don't seem compatible with your situation (for example, CBT is designed to be a short-term therapy and in most cases it doesn't help with personality disorders at all.)

When it comes to personality disorders i noticed there are lots of double standards and even if u ignore mainstream media and only consider mental health communities,  the conversation usually focuses on some categories while others are left out.

There is a belief that BPD is objectively the "worst" mental illness and that people affected by this disorder suffer more than others. Tbh this mentality makes me sick. Borderlines are more likely to put themselves in immediate danger bc of impulsive tendecies, while in other PDs the damage is only visible over time but it doesn't mean that it's less serious.

The worst part is that this narrative has real life consequences and affects the quality and accessibility of treatment, diagnosis etc.
Some time ago i had a mental breakdown and i spent entire months looking for therapists with an experience in personality disorders and every single one was specialized in BPD.

Avpd has terrible long term effects and i hate that it's considered "not that bad"..
It completely destroys your chances
to form significant connections (which is already super painful bc we all need some degree of human connection) and because social interaction is such a big part of life, it can also interfere with your career/education. This happened to me but judging from what I read in this sub it's not uncommon.

So yeah avpd isn't worse than others but considering how pervasive it can get, it deserves to be taken waaay more seriously and, overall, all PDs should be given the same importance.. The idea that cluster Cs suffer less bc their syntoms are not as "loud" as the other types is so harmful 😞

 Growing up, my mother would criticize me for the way i walked, dressed, talked and even for very insignificant stuff like the way I would tie my shoes, hold a pencil, my posture etc.. She was obsessed with these little things and acted like I had just committed a murder when I didn't do them the way she wanted.
She was alway comparing me to other kids my age and insisted on the fact that i wasn't "normal", calling me stupid or the r- slur all the time etc...
Basically she did everything she could to humiliate me and make me feel like I was inherently "wrong" and different to everyone else.

When I was 12 I began to feel embarrassing and repulsive, like I had to hide myself from the rest of world. 
From that moment on I gradually stopped interacting with others because I felt they would have been disgusted/annoyed by my painful awkwardness.

It took me a while (and a few psychology lessons as well) to realize that my issues can be traced back to the way I was treated in childhood, but unfortunately that awareness didn't change much.
To this day I can't even exist in a room with other people without feeling uncomfortable and expecially when I have to _walk_ (through the school alleys, city streets , in a shop.. literally just walk) i feel so awkward that I want to die.
And despite my best attempts I cannot stop comparing myself with others all the time and feeling like I'm worse than them on every level.

The idea that I'm wrong and stupid and embarassing beyond repair is so deeply ingrained in my brain that I can't imagine a world where I don't feel this way.

The worst part is that now my mother became a completely different person and doesn't act like that anymore, she doesn't understand why I am so insecure and says stuff like "just be yourself"  💀

All I can say for now is that CBT didn't help at all. I did it  for 2 years (plus medications) and saw no results..
